NOFA OVERVIEW AND GENERAL INFORMATION
Opportunity
The City of Long Beach Department of Community Development (City) announces the
availability of approximately $3.5 million in Community Development Block Grant
Program ( CDBG) funds to be awarded to qualified Community Land Trusts , housing
development companies, nonprofit organizations , and/or community development
corporations. Preference will be given for Community Land Trust applicants with a
demonstrated commitment to long-term affordability and community stewardship. Eligible
activities are limited to the acquisition of land for the future development of affordable
rental housing, and acquisition and rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental housing in
the City of Long Beach to add affordability restrictions for persons earning at or below
80% of the Los Angeles County Area Median Income (AMI).
Available Funding
The funding made available through this NOFA will be accessible for projects that meet
the requirements of this NOFA made through a competitive process.
Multiple projects may be awarded funds, for a total of approximately $3.5 million. The City
reserves the right to fund selected projects with an alternative funding source, including
HOME Investment Partnerships Program, Permanent Local Housing Allocation Program
(PLHA), Los Angeles County Affordable Housing Solutions Agency (LACAHSA), or other
eligible local, state, or federal funds, subject to the availability of funding.
As appropriate, f inancial assistance to selected projects will be made in the form of a
residual receipt loan. The rates and terms of the loans shall be subject to negotiations on
a project-by-project basis. All loans will be secured by a lien on the property. There are
no grant funds available under this NOFA, all funding will be in the form of a loan that
must be repaid to the City.
The deadline for submitting proposals in response to the NOFA is 4:00 P.M. on July 30,
2026. Proposals will be reviewed for compliance with the CDBG Program regulations
and the terms of this NOFA. Proposals that are determined to comply with both the CDBG
Program Regulations and the NOFA will be evaluated according to the established NOFA
Evaluation Criteria.
The proposal(s) determined to be the most competitive will be presented to the Long
Beach Community Investment Company (LBCIC) for confirmation and loan approval. The
